question.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{2x{y}^{2}-1}{{x}^{2}y}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{2h(x,y)}{{x}^{3}y}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{2x{y}^{2}-1}{{x}^{2}y}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}-1)\cdot {x}^{2}y-(2x{y}^{2}-1)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)}{({x}^{2}y)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{y}^{2}\cdot {x}^{2}y-(2x{y}^{2}-1)\cdot 2xy}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}{y}^{3}-4{x}^{2}{y}^{3}+2xy}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2xy-2{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2xy(1-x{y}^{2})}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2(1-x{y}^{2})}{{x}^{3}y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
h(x,y)=1-x{y}^{2}.
$$
